value.lineage: KISS FFT (2003-, Borgerding): a mixed-radix Cooley-Tukey FFT small enough to read in one sitting; the 'keep it simple' counterpoint to FFTW's code generation

value.built_to: compute the discrete Fourier transform (and inverse) for arbitrary sizes via mixed-radix Cooley-Tukey, in minimal readable C
value.pressure: the O(N^2) cost of the naive DFT; the demand for a small dependency-free FFT where FFTW is overkill
value.success_means: forward-then-inverse reconstructs the input within floating-point tolerance; agreement with a reference DFT

ANCESTRY.value: KISS FFT (2003-, Borgerding): a mixed-radix Cooley-Tukey FFT small enough to read in one sitting; the 'keep it simple' counterpoint to FFTW's code generation

cut.note: a mixed-radix decimation-in-time FFT in three parts: a factorisation of n that prefers 4, then 2, then odd primes; a recursion that computes p sub-transforms of size m on strided input and recombines them with a butterfly for the radix; and a single precomputed twiddle table indexed by stride; the whole transform is 420 lines and its stated purpose is to be readable

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: kf_factor (307-336): p = 4 -> 2 -> 3, 5, 7, ...; if p > floor(sqrt(n)) then p = n; facbuf = p1, m1, p2, m2, ...
organs.mechanism: starting with 4, divide out that radix while it divides n, then fall to 2, then step through odd numbers; whenever the candidate exceeds the square root of the remainder, the remainder itself becomes the last radix (a prime, handled by the generic butterfly); the factor list is stored as (radix, sub-length) pairs consumed by the recursion
assumptions: radix-4 stages are the cheapest per point among the hard-coded butterflies, so they are taken first; any n is allowed, with primes paying O(p^2) in the generic stage
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: arbitrary lengths with the best hard-coded stages used first
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a large prime length costs O(n^2) (kiss_fft_next_fast_size exists so callers can pad to 2^a 3^b 5^c)

organs.human_name: kf_work (236-306): p, m from the factor list; the m == 1 base case copies strided input; the recursive call with fstride * p; the switch to kf_bfly2/3/4/5/generic
organs.mechanism: for a stage with radix p and sub-length m: if m is 1 copy the p strided input points; else call itself p times on input offset by k * stride to fill p contiguous blocks of m outputs (the sub-transforms), then apply the radix-p butterfly across the blocks; the stride multiplies by p at each level so the decimation is expressed by pointer arithmetic, not by a bit-reversal permutation
organs.input: strided input, the factor list, the twiddles
organs.output: the transform in place in Fout
assumptions: Cooley-Tukey: a length p*m DFT is p DFTs of length m on decimated input followed by m radix-p DFTs with twiddles; recursion on the factor list makes mixed radix natural
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no bit reversal, no scratch beyond the output, one code path for every radix
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: recursion depth equals the number of factors (small); the OpenMP branch parallelises only the top level
organs.human_prior: Cooley & Tukey 1965; the recursive strided form is common in small FFTs (also FFTW's codelets)

organs.human_name: kf_bfly2 (15-37): t = Fout2 * tw; Fout2 = Fout - t; Fout += t; tw advances by fstride; kiss_fft_alloc (337-370): twiddles[i] = exp(-2 pi i k / n) for the whole n; kf_bfly_generic (192, not read)
organs.mechanism: one table of n twiddles for the full length is computed at plan time; a stage with stride s reads every s-th entry, which is exactly the twiddle set for that stage's sub-length; the radix-2 butterfly multiplies the second half by the twiddle and forms sum and difference in place; radices 3, 4 and 5 have hand-written equivalents; other primes use a generic loop that multiplies every input by every twiddle power (O(p^2)); the fixed-point build divides by the radix at each stage to prevent overflow (C_FIXDIV)
assumptions: the twiddles of every stage are a stride-subset of the length-n table (true because every sub-length divides n)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one table, no per-stage tables, and the hot loops are a page of arithmetic
organs.source_boundary: the bfly functions and the table setup (3/4/5/generic bodies not read)

rejected_cuts.candidate: kiss_fftr.c (real-input transform by a half-length complex FFT and a post-twiddle), kiss_fftnd.c (multi-dimensional by row-column), the fixed-point and SIMD macros, the tools (fastfir, psdpng)
rejected_cuts.note: the real-input trick is a small mechanism of its own

rejected_cuts.evidence: factorisation, recursion and butterflies are separately replaceable (FFTW replaces all three with generated codelets and a planner)

pressures.condition: an organism must transform vectors of lengths chosen by the world (including odd and composite ones); the score is time per transform and the size of the organism (lines, tables) it needs; an O(n^2) DFT is the baseline
pressures.resource_or_constraint: one twiddle table; no code generation
pressures.failure_condition: O(n^2) on composite lengths, or a wrong result on a length with an odd factor
pressures.world_punishes: power-of-two-only transforms; per-stage tables; bit-reversal bookkeeping
pressures.world_rewards: mixed-radix recursion with strided twiddle reuse
pressures.observable_consequence: time vs n for n in {2^k, 2^a 3^b 5^c, primes} against the direct DFT and against a generated-codelet FFT (FFTW) on the same host; max error vs the direct DFT
pressures.vacuity_condition: n a power of two only
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: padding to a power of two (which changes the transform)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the direct DFT must match it to round-off; the organism on a prime length must show the O(p^2) fallback; a power-of-two length must show the radix-4 stages dominating: the world must show all three

ancestry_edges.to: Cooley & Tukey 1965 (mixed radix); the strided recursive form
ancestry_edges.note: from the README and the source
